novelty_flags.label: comparator_promise_table / BoegeSolus2024
novelty_flags.one_line: The core attributes the positive-denominator birational result to “Theorem 3.15” of arXiv:2410.23102v1, but that version identifies Theorem 3.10 as its main result and Theorem 3.11 as the saturation result.

novelty_flags.label: thm:bounded-width-compiler and oeq:positive-real-compiler
novelty_flags.one_line: The omitted close comparator Wu, Zhu, Goharshady, An, Xia, and Zhan (TACAS 2026), Quantifier Elimination Meets Treewidth, gives tree-decomposition dynamic programming for CAD/QE; the proposal must compare its custom width and certificate promise against that result.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: covariance theorems and oeq:positive-real-compiler
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Claims are restricted to theorem-specific variance-active generic loci and make no pointwise assertion on true variance-neutral hyperplanes.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All covariance-frontier conclusions are conditional on the stated generic chamber and do not cover t_k=v_k.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: project_justification / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The new chamberwise class Cov_p(G) is not asserted to equal, contain, or be contained in the paper's published soft2(G) class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The headline is a result about the newly defined robust chamberwise frontier, informed by but not settling Problem 5.2's containments.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: sampling_model
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Aligned factorization data are explicit population inputs; their recovery from raw laws and finite-sample behavior are outside scope.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Identification is conditional on the aligned population factorization datum and covariance tuple.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1, abstract and introduction, especially lines naming Theorems 3.10 and 3.11
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The version states that positive denominators support its birational implicitization result, identifies Theorem 3.10 as the main result, and identifies Theorem 3.11 as the saturation result; it has no cited Theorem 3.15.

Add Wu et al. (TACAS 2026) as the primary algorithmic comparator and prove whether covariance-terminal width bounds, is bounded by, or is incomparable with its formula-primal treewidth; state which realization/separator guarantee remains unavailable from its CAD/QE framework.

Promote the bounded-width result from a generic compiler claim to a strict comparative theorem by exhibiting an infinite family where the proposed certificate is available with the stated output semantics while the published low-treewidth QE formulation does not directly certify graph-frontier membership.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two published-literature comparisons, especially the missing treewidth-QE comparator, then continue to Stage 0 with the field-tier terminal correction and bounded-width compiler targets.
